scenes.tts: If three kinds of taste cell send the same chemical signal, how does the brain tell them apart?
scenes.visual: Three taste cells, sweet, umami and bitter, each sending an identical signal to a nerve fibre. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: If three kinds of taste cell send the same chemical signal, how does the brain tell them apart?

scenes.tts: In the taste bud, type two cells detect sweet, umami and bitter.
scenes.visual: A taste bud; the type II cells highlighted and labelled sweet, umami, bitter.
scenes.caption: In the taste bud, type II cells detect sweet, umami and bitter.
scenes.narration: In the taste bud, type II cells detect sweet, umami and bitter.

scenes.tts: Sweet and umami cells carry T one R receptors. Bitter cells carry T two R receptors.
scenes.visual: Receptor icons: T1R2 with T1R3 on sweet cells, T1R1 with T1R3 on umami cells, many T2Rs on bitter cells.
scenes.caption: Sweet and umami cells carry T1R receptors. Bitter cells carry T2R receptors.
scenes.narration: Sweet and umami cells carry T1R receptors. Bitter cells carry T2R receptors.

scenes.tts: After the receptor, all three use the same steps.
scenes.visual: The three cells drawn side by side with an identical chain of four labelled steps inside each.
scenes.narration: After the receptor, all three use the same steps.

scenes.tts: An enzyme, PLC beta two, leads to a calcium rise. Calcium opens a channel, and the cell depolarizes.
scenes.visual: Chain steps light in order: PLCβ2, IP3R3, TRPM5, CALHM1/3.
scenes.caption: An enzyme, PLCβ2, leads to a calcium rise. Calcium opens a channel, and the cell depolarizes.
scenes.narration: An enzyme, PLCβ2, leads to a calcium rise. Calcium opens a channel, and the cell depolarizes.

scenes.tts: Then ATP flows out through a channel onto the nerve fibre.
scenes.visual: ATP particles flow out of the cell through a channel onto the nerve fibre.
scenes.narration: Then ATP flows out through a channel onto the nerve fibre.

scenes.tts: So the signal is the same. The rule's answer: what differs is which cell the nerve listens to.
scenes.visual: Arrows run from each cell to the nerve. Text: which cell the nerve listens to.
scenes.narration: So the signal is the same. The rule's answer: what differs is which cell the nerve listens to.

scenes.tts: Zhang and colleagues deleted PLC beta two from the whole mouse.
scenes.visual: A mouse; the PLCβ2 step crossed out in all three type II cells. Caption: Zhang and colleagues, 2003.
scenes.caption: Zhang and colleagues deleted PLCβ2 from the whole mouse.
scenes.narration: Zhang and colleagues deleted PLCβ2 from the whole mouse.

scenes.tts: Nerve responses to the tested sweet, amino-acid and bitter stimuli were lost. In lick tests, sweet preference was strongly reduced, and bitter avoidance was lost.
scenes.visual: Sweet, umami and bitter cells go dark. A mouse at a lick spout shows little preference for sweet and no avoidance of bitter.
scenes.narration: Nerve responses to the tested sweet, amino-acid and bitter stimuli were lost. In lick tests, sweet preference was strongly reduced, and bitter avoidance was lost.

scenes.tts: Sour and salty responses remained, because those cells use other routes.
scenes.visual: Sour and salt cells stay lit.
scenes.narration: Sour and salty responses remained, because those cells use other routes.

scenes.tts: Then they put it back only in cells with bitter receptors.
scenes.visual: The PLCβ2 step is restored in the bitter cell only.
scenes.narration: Then they put it back only in cells with bitter receptors.

scenes.tts: Which responses come back? Bitter only, all three, or none?
scenes.visual: Three empty checkboxes under sweet, umami and bitter. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Which responses come back? Bitter only, all three, or none?

scenes.tts: Bitter only, in the nerve and in behaviour. Sweet and amino-acid responses did not return.
scenes.visual: The bitter cell lights; sweet and umami stay dark. The mouse avoids a bitter solution again.
scenes.narration: Bitter only, in the nerve and in behaviour. Sweet and amino-acid responses did not return.

scenes.tts: The shared enzyme works only for its own cell's quality. The lines are separate.
scenes.visual: Label: each cell is a separate line to the nerve.
scenes.narration: The shared enzyme works only for its own cell's quality. The lines are separate.

scenes.tts: Does the cell also decide what a line means? Put a receptor in the wrong cell.
scenes.visual: A bitter receptor icon hovers over a sweet cell.
scenes.narration: Does the cell also decide what a line means? Put a receptor in the wrong cell.

scenes.tts: Mueller and colleagues put a human bitter receptor into the sweet cells of mice.
scenes.visual: The bitter receptor inserts into the sweet cell's membrane. Caption: Mueller and colleagues, 2005.
scenes.narration: Mueller and colleagues put a human bitter receptor into the sweet cells of mice.

scenes.tts: Its ligand is a bitter compound that normal mice ignore. Will these mice avoid it, or drink it?
scenes.visual: Two bottles side by side: the ligand solution and water. A mouse with T2R16 in its sweet cells stands between them; beside it a control mouse samples both bottles without preference. Question on screen: avoid or drink?
scenes.narration: Its ligand is a bitter compound that normal mice ignore. Will these mice avoid it, or drink it?

scenes.tts: They drink it, while normal mice stay indifferent. The receptor detects the molecule, but the sweet cell decides what that means.
scenes.visual: The T2R16 mouse drinks mostly from the ligand bottle; the control mouse samples both bottles equally, with no preference. Label: sweet-cell activation drives attraction; this is not a report of subjective sweetness.
scenes.narration: They drink it, while normal mice stay indifferent. The receptor detects the molecule, but the sweet cell decides what that means.

scenes.tts: In mouse taste, each kind of cell acts like a labeled line.
scenes.visual: The sweet cell's output wire tagged SWEET, whatever receptor is on it.
scenes.narration: In mouse taste, each kind of cell acts like a labeled line.

scenes.tts: One consequence: a bitter cell pools many receptors. By its rate alone, that cell cannot say which bitter compound it met.
scenes.visual: Two different bitter molecules each activate one bitter cell equally; its single output is identical. Label: one cell.
scenes.narration: One consequence: a bitter cell pools many receptors. By its rate alone, that cell cannot say which bitter compound it met.

scenes.tts: Not every bitter cell carries the same receptors, so the pathway may keep some distinctions. Still, pooling fits a sense that mostly answers: eat it, or reject it?
scenes.visual: Split screen: many smell lines beside a few bitter cells, each with a different receptor mix, feeding one choice: eat or reject.
scenes.narration: Not every bitter cell carries the same receptors, so the pathway may keep some distinctions. Still, pooling fits a sense that mostly answers: eat it, or reject it?

scenes.tts: Keep the scope. These are mouse experiments on the periphery. Some taste cells and nerve cells respond to more than one quality.
scenes.visual: Scope card: mouse periphery; some cells respond to more than one quality.
scenes.narration: Keep the scope. These are mouse experiments on the periphery. Some taste cells and nerve cells respond to more than one quality.

scenes.tts: Smell reads a pattern across many lines. Taste reads mainly which kind of cell is active.
scenes.visual: Final card: Smell reads a pattern across many lines. Taste reads mainly which kind of cell is active.
scenes.narration: Smell reads a pattern across many lines. Taste reads mainly which kind of cell is active.
